fastembed_local.route: TextEmbedding(model_name=..., specific_model_path=<dir>) with add_custom_model(pooling=MEAN, normalization=True, model_file='model_tokens.onnx')
fastembed_local.finding: fastembed applies its OWN declared pooling to the model output, so it cannot accept a graph that has already pooled -- and its pipeline has no slot for a dense layer AFTER pooling, which is exactly where nano's head sits. Masked mean-pooling is linear, so mean(W.h_i + b) == W.mean(h_i) + b: exporting the head PER TOKEN and letting fastembed pool is identical, not an approximation. Measured, not assumed.
fastembed_local.consequence_for_m10: nano ships TWO graphs from one set of weights -- a self-contained model.onnx for anyone calling ONNX Runtime directly, and model_tokens.onnx for fastembed. They agree to 6e-08.
